blocks.x: Quantum & Advanced Compute applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Energy & Utilities, quantum & advanced compute is the frontier tower, run with a pragmatist's discipline. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: quantum readiness & strategy, quantum optimization for enterprise problems, post-quantum cryptography migration — delivered on Dataq Quanta and Dataq Sentinel with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Substations and pipelines outlive cryptographic eras; long-lived keys and protocols face PQ exposure with no inventory or clock.
Renewable supply and flexible demand make legacy forecasting blind; imbalance costs and curtailment climb while forecasts run on yesterday's methods.
IT/OT convergence, remote access growth and legacy SCADA estates create attack paths with physical consequences; CIP/NIS2 duties expand faster than programs mature.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

The delivery pattern composes 6 services from the Quantum & Advanced Compute tower — Quantum Readiness & Strategy, Quantum Optimization for Enterprise Problems, Post-Quantum Cryptography Migration, Quantum Machine Learning & Simulation as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method with sector controls: CSRD / ISSB obligations shape the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: A quantum plan that survives a CFO: inventory, risk clocks and sequenced roadmaps.
Routing, scheduling, portfolios and formulations: hybrid solvers beating classical baselines.
Beat the harvest-now-decrypt-later clock: cryptographic inventory to PQC cutover.
QML and simulation pilots with industrial honesty: real baselines, real data, real verdicts.
Classical vs. Quantum-inspired solvers on scheduling formulations (solve time and quality gains where hybrids win)
CBOM across substations and control systems (migration sequenced over asset lifetimes)

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: CSRD / ISSB and DORA / NIS2. Operational resilience and cyber duties for essential entities. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Delivery follows the same weekly rhythm on every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
